channel_name: Real Vision · Raoul Pal - The journey man
video_title: Solana, Tokenized Stocks, and Backpack w/ Armani Ferrante | Raoul Pal The Journey Man
gist: Backpack founder Armani Ferrante argues crypto's next leg of asset growth comes from bringing the regulated economy on-chain via licensed, compliance-first intermediaries, with Backpack aiming to take tokenized, 1:1 redeemable stocks on Solana from ~200 symbols to ~10,000. Raoul Pal and Ferrante also frame blockchains as a 'global API for finance', see an agentic economy needing crypto rails for capital, and pitch prediction markets as intelligence/forecasting instruments rather than gambling.

insights.claim: Armani Ferrante expects crypto to grow 100x, with that growth coming from the industry's maturation (compliance, national adoption, RWAs, tokenized stocks, stablecoins) rather than from the 'wild west' segment of the market.
insights.speaker: Armani Ferrante
insights.so_what: Favors exposure to compliant, licensed crypto infrastructure and RWA/tokenization plays over purely speculative DeFi.
insights.quote: crypto is not dead. It's going to grow 100x and all of that growth is not going to come from the old world of you know you know the wild west of the industry

insights.claim: Ferrante believes the core crypto story of the next couple of years is bringing the world's regulated economy on-chain, and that this is where all asset growth in crypto will come from.
insights.speaker: Armani Ferrante
insights.so_what: Watch on-chain tokenized-asset AUM and licensed onramps as the leading indicator of the cycle, not memecoin activity.
insights.quote: It's how do you bring the entire world's regulated economy and bring it onchain and that's where all the asset growth is going to come from.

insights.claim: Licensing and compliance unlock products that pure DeFi cannot ship alone, such as US perpetual futures; the reported (leaked) Hyperliquid-Kraken partnership pairs Hyperliquid's horizontal exchange engine with Kraken's licensing layer.
insights.speaker: Armani Ferrante
insights.so_what: DeFi protocols that partner with licensed venues may gain access to US derivatives demand; licensed intermediaries hold pricing power over distribution.

insights.claim: Backpack deliberately avoided opening globally on day one post-FTX, instead pursuing country-by-country licensing (Dubai/UAE first, Europe for three years, Japan, and the US), which Ferrante says makes it less exposed to US legislative setbacks like the reportedly stalled CLARITY Act.
insights.speaker: Armani Ferrante
insights.so_what: Compliance-first exchanges are a hedge against US regulatory whipsaw; Ferrante expects agency rulemaking to deliver clarity even if the CLARITY Act dies.
insights.quote: I woke up this morning and the clarity act appears to be dead or at least that's the conversation on on Twitter.

insights.claim: Ferrante reframes crypto speculation as the ordinary risk-transfer function of all financial markets (e.g., CME hedgers need speculators on the other side), arguing 'crypto' should just be called finance.
insights.speaker: Armani Ferrante
insights.so_what: Supports the view that crypto venues will converge with mainstream finance rather than remain a separate asset silo.
insights.quote: I kind of like to just eliminate crypto for my vocabulary. It's all just finance.

insights.claim: Raoul Pal argues crypto's hyper-speculation acts as a speed-test for financial innovation, compressing what would take a decade in other markets into six months, with memecoins functioning as instant capital formation.
insights.speaker: Raoul Pal
insights.so_what: Crypto experiments (memecoins, pre-IPO tokens) are early previews of structures that later reach traditional capital markets.
insights.quote: Things that would take a decade in other markets can be done in six months in crypto.

insights.claim: Backpack's top 2026 priority is bringing the entire US stock market to Solana through one API that converts a bona fide security entitlement to and from a token, portable between DeFi and brokerages like Fidelity, Robinhood and E*Trade.
insights.speaker: Armani Ferrante
insights.so_what: If executed, full-market tokenized equities on Solana would be a major new on-chain volume and fee source for SOL and Solana DeFi.
insights.quote: We want to bring the entire stock market to Salana.

insights.claim: Only about 100-200 tokenized stock symbols exist across all chains (Robinhood chain, Ethereum, Solana); Ferrante sees the jump to ~10,000 symbols as the next big leap.
insights.speaker: Armani Ferrante
insights.so_what: Symbol coverage is a trackable metric for tokenized-equity adoption; long-tail coverage is the growth runway.
insights.quote: going from 200 symbols to 10,000 is going to be a huge jump and that's the next leap that we're going to make.

insights.claim: Backpack's tokenized stocks are minted and redeemed against shares held by a clearing broker, giving 1:1 fungibility and redeemability, which Ferrante argues makes them closer to real stocks than USDC is to cash.
insights.speaker: Armani Ferrante
insights.so_what: Redeemability design is the key differentiator among tokenized-stock issuers; open 1:1 redemption keeps token prices tethered to underlying shares.
insights.quote: tokenized stocks are probably closer to stocks than USDC is to uh cash

insights.claim: Liquidity for tokenized stocks will come from two models: bootstrapping native on-chain liquidity (capital-intensive, billions needed, viable for roughly the top 100 symbols) and bridging traditional-market liquidity via 'intent' intermediaries that source shares at the NBBO for the long tail.
insights.speaker: Armani Ferrante
insights.so_what: Market makers and intent/solver networks that bridge TradFi liquidity are key enablers to watch.

insights.claim: Ferrante sees no principled reason retail on Solana can't get the same execution and liquidity as on Robinhood, E*Trade or Fidelity; on-chain price discovery via order books is a later stage, with retail flow bootstrapping the market first.
insights.speaker: Armani Ferrante
insights.so_what: Pushes back on the 'thin crypto liquidity' objection Raoul Pal raised (HFTs/Citadel not yet active on-chain) for retail-size trading.

insights.claim: In the dispute between the AMC CEO and Robinhood CEO Vlad over tokenized stocks, Ferrante argues tokenization is overwhelmingly positive for listed companies because it brings net new capital inflows into their stock.
insights.speaker: Armani Ferrante
insights.so_what: Expect issuer pushback on tokenization to fade as CEOs recognize it as incremental global demand for their shares.
insights.quote: You have more capital flowing into your company rather than less capital.

insights.claim: Ferrante calls Robinhood chain probably the most exciting crypto ecosystem to emerge from nothing over the past cycle, and Raoul Pal notes Robinhood is moving with startup-like speed that can force industry change.
insights.speaker: Armani Ferrante
insights.so_what: Robinhood (HOOD) is a scale incumbent driving tokenized-equity adoption; a competitor and validator for Solana-based efforts.
insights.quote: Robin Hood chain's definitely been probably the most exciting crypto ecosystem to come out of nothing over the past, you know, cycle.

insights.claim: Raoul Pal argues tokenized US equities, like stablecoins as an extension of the eurodollar market, will channel global flow of funds into US dollar assets and increase US financial dominance while letting anyone anywhere own fractional US stocks.
insights.speaker: Raoul Pal
insights.so_what: Tokenization is structurally bullish for USD demand and for US equity valuations via widened global access.
insights.quote: The stable coins are like an extension of the Euro dollar markets.

insights.claim: Tokenized pre-IPO equities and pre-IPO perpetual futures are opening private-company exposure (e.g., Anthropic, SpaceX) to non-accredited investors; Ferrante warns that once billions trade on pre-IPO tokens, pre-emptive price discovery will affect IPOs themselves, and that crypto shows misaligned incentives when tokens launch too early.
insights.speaker: Armani Ferrante
insights.so_what: Pre-IPO token prices may become reference marks for IPO pricing and compress VC-to-public upside; watch for early-launch incentive problems.
insights.quote: What is an IPO at this point? The structure of markets changes really fast.

themes.theme: Blockchains as a global finance API

insights.claim: Ferrante frames blockchains not as exchanges but as a global API for all of finance, where buying a stock, option, FX or sending money becomes an API call, something that had not happened for money until now.
insights.speaker: Armani Ferrante
insights.so_what: Value accrues to the base settlement layer and to distribution owners, while back-end liquidity becomes an implementation detail.
insights.quote: what all this leads to in the limit is just a global API for all of finance, right? That's really what I think these blockchains are. They're not exchanges.

insights.claim: Raoul Pal (echoing hedge fund manager Richard Galvin) and Armani Ferrante agree the user-relationship/aggregator layer (brokerages, wallets, retail front-ends) is the obvious way to participate in tokenization, because trust and compliance remain human needs even if software costs go to zero.
insights.speaker: Armani Ferrante
insights.so_what: Investable angle: owners of the customer relationship (brokerages, wallets) rather than commoditized liquidity venues.

insights.claim: Ferrante disputes Raoul Pal's view that UX layers disappear in an agent-driven world, citing the memecoin app FOMO, which built only a consumer experience on top of Solana/crypto infrastructure (no wallet, exchange, custody, chain, or licensing), as proof that abstraction lets new apps flourish.
insights.speaker: Armani Ferrante
insights.so_what: Expect an explosion of thin consumer apps on crypto rails; a lot of new app-layer launches could follow.

insights.claim: When AI can cheaply rebuild software, app-layer moats weaken, but Ferrante argues regulatory licensing and social-graph network effects (as with FOMO, Facebook, Instagram) become even stronger moats.
insights.speaker: Armani Ferrante
insights.so_what: When evaluating crypto apps, favor those with licensing depth or social graphs over pure software features.

insights.claim: Ferrante argues capital is the key prerequisite for AI agents to act in the real world, and a censorship-resistant global ledger lets AI hold a bank account (e.g., a USDC wallet) and pay humans for services.
insights.speaker: Armani Ferrante
insights.so_what: Stablecoins and permissionless chains are the likely payment rails for agent activity, a potentially large new source of on-chain demand.
insights.quote: You now have the ability for AI intelligence to actually have a bank account.

insights.claim: Ferrante contends that a censorship-resistant money layer raises the probability of AI 'doom' exponentially and is a prerequisite for superintelligence to take over, and expects this to reshape the crypto debate within 5-10 years.
insights.speaker: Armani Ferrante
insights.so_what: A potential future regulatory/political overhang on permissionless crypto that the market has not priced.
insights.quote: I would say that money layer is a prerequisite for super intelligence to take over the world.

insights.claim: Raoul Pal cites Solana co-founder Raj saying roughly 240,000 tokens launch per day (likely mostly agents), and expects AI agents to spin up short-lived tokens and businesses, extracting profit from an idea in a week and shutting down.
insights.speaker: Raoul Pal
insights.so_what: Token-launch volumes may increasingly reflect agent rather than human activity; relevant for launchpad and chain fee metrics.
insights.quote: they've got 240,000 tokens launch a day. I'm like are these humans or are these agents? He's like I don't know but I think it's agents

insights.claim: Raoul Pal says his measures show AI intelligence per dollar or per joule doubling every 4.2 months and argues no one, including Anthropic or OpenAI, can regulate or restrain it.
insights.speaker: Raoul Pal
insights.so_what: Pal's exponential-age thesis underpins his bullishness on AI plus crypto convergence.
insights.quote: We're doubling every 4.2 months. It's bananas.

insights.claim: Raoul Pal expects an 'invisible economy' of data marketplaces for AI agents that tokenizes the world's trapped data, which he believes will be bigger than the existing financial marketplace.
insights.speaker: Raoul Pal
insights.so_what: Points to data-tokenization protocols as a possible next frontier beyond financial RWAs.
insights.quote: I just think that marketplace is bigger than the existing financial marketplace.

insights.claim: Ferrante argues prediction markets are closer to futures contracts and superforecaster platforms than gambling, and are expanding from sports toward forecasting company earnings and the price of Bitcoin.
insights.speaker: Armani Ferrante
insights.so_what: The addressable market is larger than sports betting; watch expansion into earnings/macro contracts.

insights.claim: Raoul Pal argues prediction markets combined with internet scale, an effectively infinite TAM from AI agents, and blockchains as the ledger make them a much bigger opportunity than the market understands.
insights.speaker: Raoul Pal
insights.so_what: Supports long-term bullishness on prediction-market platforms and the chains they settle on.
insights.quote: then you add in an infinite TAM from agents and then you add in blockchain as the ledger system for it all. Okay, that's something a lot bigger than people still understand.

insights.claim: Backpack lost $14.5 million, its entire runway, in the FTX collapse, yet Ferrante stayed on Solana because he judged its fundamentals completely disconnected from the news-cycle hysteria.
insights.speaker: Armani Ferrante
insights.so_what: Illustrates the playbook of buying/building into ecosystem capitulation when on-the-ground fundamentals diverge from sentiment.
insights.quote: the fundamentals completely disconnected from the hysteria of the news cycle

insights.claim: Ferrante's reasoning for Solana: if crypto matters, a high-throughput, low-latency chain is required, and post-FTX Solana was the only such chain with a mature startup ecosystem (e.g., projects like Pyth and Wormhole).
insights.speaker: Armani Ferrante
insights.so_what: A reusable logic chain for picking L1 winners: throughput requirement plus ecosystem depth.
insights.quote: Slaughter was really the only game in town.
